research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has continuous (non-intermittent) demand on most working days with high but not extreme variability, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy more efficient than periodic review. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs optimally given the low unit cost and high ordering cost ratio. The storage cap constrains Q below the pure EOQ but the policy remains feasible.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage constraint is active: safety_stock (1,190) + order_quantity (5,365) = 6,555, exactly at the 6,556-unit cap. Any upward revision of safety stock (e.g., in response to a demand spike) would require a corresponding reduction in order quantity, potentially increasing ordering frequency and cost. Close monitoring of actual inventory peaks is advised.
